task1: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of portal tracts that are normal in size and architecture, without expansion or dense inflammatory cuffing. The portal-lobular interface is sharp and well-defined.
task2: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of interlobular bile ducts with smooth, regular contours, not surrounded or distorted by a prominent inflammatory infiltrate.
task3: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of central and portal veins with thin, non-inflamed walls. There is no perivenular cuffing of inflammatory cells or associated parenchymal reaction.

task1: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of a few portal tracts containing mild inflammatory infiltrates, without significant expansion of the portal tract boundaries. The overall lobular architecture remains intact.
task2: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of a minority of interlobular bile ducts being surrounded and slightly distorted by a rim of inflammatory cells, while most bile ducts appear architecturally normal.
task3: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of subtle inflammatory cuffing around a minority of portal or central veins, without significant parenchymal reaction.

task1: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of the majority or all portal tracts being expanded by a dense mixed inflammatory infiltrate, causing obvious widening of the portal areas. The presence of numerous eosinophils may be suggested by patchy, intense staining.
task2: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of the majority of interlobular bile ducts being prominently cuffed and infiltrated by inflammatory cells, leading to visible distortion and irregularity of the ductal contours.
task3: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of prominent inflammatory cuffing around the majority of portal and/or central veins. There may be focal dropout of hepatocytes immediately surrounding some central veins.

task1: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of severely expanded and edematous portal tracts due to dense inflammation. The inflammatory cells spill out from the portal tracts into the surrounding periportal hepatic parenchyma, blurring the portal-lobular interface.
task2: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of widespread bile duct damage, with many ducts showing degenerative changes or even focal disruption of the ductal lumen, appearing fragmented or absent.
task3: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at low resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of severe central vein inflammation extending into the surrounding parenchyma, forming a confluent zone of necrosis or dropout that may bridge between central veins.

task1: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of portal tracts containing only scattered, occasional resident lymphocytes or histiocytes within the stroma, without evidence of a dense or activated inflammatory infiltrate. The limiting plate is intact.
task2: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of interlobular bile ducts with normal epithelial morphology. The biliary epithelial cells are cuboidal with basally located nuclei, normal nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, and no evidence of intra-epithelial lymphocytic infiltration or degenerative changes.
task3: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of central and portal veins with an intact, flattened endothelial lining. There are no inflammatory cells adherent to or beneath the endothelium (no subendothelial infiltration). The perivenular hepatocytes are preserved.

task1: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of scattered lymphocytes and other mononuclear inflammatory cells infiltrating a minority of portal tracts. The portal stroma is not expanded, and the limiting plate is sharp.
task2: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of inflammatory cells, primarily lymphocytes, infiltrating the epithelium of a few interlobular bile ducts. The biliary epithelial cells show reactive changes such as increased nuclear size and nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, but maintain overall polarity.
task3: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of lymphocytes adherent to and lifting up the endothelium (subendothelial infiltration) in a few interlobular and/or central veins. The underlying hepatocytes are preserved.

task1: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of a mixed inflammatory infiltrate within most portal tracts, comprising lymphocytes, plasma cells, and occasional neutrophils and eosinophils. Portal edema and swollen microvascular endothelial cells may be present, raising consideration for acute antibody-mediated rejection.
task2: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of dense inflammatory infiltration within the epithelium of most bile ducts. The biliary epithelial cells exhibit marked degenerative changes, including nuclear pleomorphism, loss of polarity, and cytoplasmic vacuolization.
task3: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of subendothelial inflammatory cell infiltration in most interlobular and/or central veins. There is focal dropout (loss) of perivenular hepatocytes adjacent to some central veins.

task1: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of a dense, mixed portal inflammatory infiltrate that breaches the limiting plate, extending into the periportal zone (interface activity). Individual inflammatory cells, including lymphocytes and granulocytes, are seen infiltrating the periportal hepatocytes.
task2: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of advanced degenerative changes in the majority of bile ducts, including epithelial attenuation, pyknosis, and focal destruction of the ductal lumen. The basement membrane may be disrupted.
task3: A WSI of liver transplant biopsy at high resolution with visually descriptive characteristics of severe central venulitis with extensive subendothelial inflammation. The inflammation extends into the perivenular zone (central perivenulitis), accompanied by confluent or bridging necrosis of the majority of surrounding hepatocytes.
